units.translation: where Blomfield says: "πρόπου-μνος [before the stern]. πρόπρυμνος ἐκβολὴ [a jettison from the stern] is a loss which happens from the stern. Of course, goods were thrown out from the stern. Stanley well compared Acts of the Apostles 27, 18. He did not compare Ag. 1010 καὶ τὸ μὲν πρὸ χρη-μάτων κτησίων ὄκνος βαλὼν σφενδόνας ἀπ᾿ εὐ-μέτρου, οὐκ ἔδυ πρόπας δόμος οὐδ᾽ ἐπόντισε σκάφος [and the hesitation before acquired wealth, casting slings from a well-measured distance, did not sink the whole house nor swamp the ship]." Stephanus records another interpretation in Thes. vol. 3 p. 1825 in these words: "πρό-πρυμνα [utterly] from Aeschylus' Sept. is cited for funditus, prorsus, penitus [utterly, wholly, completely]". If this interpretation were correct, πρόπρεμνα [root and branch] would have to be written, as Wecklein in Studien zu Aeschylus p. 64, since πρέμνοθεν [from the root] in two places in Aeschylus has been corrupted into πρυμνόθεν [from the stern].

But the word ἐκβολάν [jettison] is evidence that Aeschylus used a metaphor drawn from naval matters, which the scholiast understood, whose annotation we have placed under the word ἐκβολή [jettison] p. 110. To this, however, is suited
But wealth of men who eat bread, grown too fat, brings jettison from the stern.

a preposition construed with the genitive, dative, and accusative.
πρός with the genitive: from, with local meaning
πρός τινος εἶναι is said of what suits someone's character or morals.
πρός with the genitive, signifying the person through whom or by whose authority something is done
Or the person from whom something proceeds
Much more frequently πρός is joined with passive verbs,
πρός with intransitive verbs.
2. πρός with the dative: at, near, by.
πρός with the dative: besides, in addition, beyond.
3. πρός with the accusative: towards.

Of the end, purpose, or reason for which something is done,
πρὸς ταῦτα and πρὸς τάδε: as to these things, therefore.
πρός with accusatives of substantives has the force of a simple dative or of adverbs.
4. πρός without a case, adverbially: besides, moreover.
